title: The Stranger
tagline: Why prompts work — three levers, sixty-four hand-written answers, zero network
hub_blurb: Change one prompt lever at a time—context, a success specification, or expert vocabulary—and see exactly what each contributes.
card_blurb: A question sits beside three toggleable levers, and the answer changes in exactly one dimension per lever. Sixty-four hand-written answers, a deck that decides your answer’s shape whenever you don’t, and a meter counting the expert vocabulary you got for free.
description: **The Stranger** — why prompts work, for a classroom. A student's question sits beside three toggleable blocks — context, success spec, expert keywords — and all 64 answers across four scenarios are hand-written answers baked into the file, ~25,700 words, with a gate that fails the build if any two share more than 5% of their sentences. The levers-off answers are deliberately competent and aimed at nobody, so the room cannot dismiss the demo as rigged. Two stage mechanics: a target deck living inside lever 2 that deals itself a card whenever nobody has said what a finished answer looks like, and a jargon meter that counts the expert terms the student never typed (0–4 with the keyword lever off, 15–20 with it on). Class scoring plots usefulness against levers pulled, plus a self-paced student walkthrough with quizzes. Includes a printable presenter sheet and eight cut-out target cards.
